display.title: The Honest Thief
display.summary_short: A poor, unlucky Jew is promised a hidden treasure by a tzaddik, and finds it by refusing to steal, even when a disguised sheriff pressures him.
display.summary_long: Sometimes we must do what we are told even when we do not understand why. Shlemiel, a poor and clumsy man in a Polish shtetl, cannot keep a job, and his children go hungry. A visiting tzaddik tells him a great treasure awaits him in Heaven but will not say how he will get it. Walking through the empty marketplace at night, Shlemiel finds a store left unlocked; tempted by the yetzer hara, he takes exactly 18 pennies from the open money box for a loaf of bread, writes down the debt, and leaves the rest. Night after night the same thing happens, and the town buzzes about the "honest thief." The sheriff, disguised as a drunken beggar, catches him and demands that he climb into the sheriff's own house and steal a newly inherited treasure. Shlemiel refuses to keep any of it, climbs in, and overhears a servant plotting to poison the sheriff's tea. He warns the "beggar," who turns out to be the sheriff himself. The grateful sheriff insists on giving him half the treasure. Shlemiel repays every 18 pennies, gives tzedakah, and understands the tzaddik's silence: his riches came through resisting temptation.
display.lesson: Trust the ways of Hashem even when we do not understand them; overcoming the temptation to take what is not ours brings blessing.
